subject: Calling a model outside of stan

messages.author: 82e8106f84fe4fab
messages.subject: Calling a model outside of stan
parts:
Hi all,

2 quick questions
1) I am thinking of running stan on a physical model that has been compiled into an executable file. Basically, I am hoping to change the input file to the executable (text file) using the samples generated and run the executable but I can't find any examples to do this. Hence I would like to ask if there is any way to run an executable file from within the Stan model block? 
2) Since I can run an executable from R, I was wondering if it is possible to call an R function (that runs the executable) from within the Stan model block.

Any suggestions or work arounds would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Calling a model outside of stan
parts:
Hi Adrian,

I wish I could help you, but I don't understand your questions. Perhaps if you could be clearer? Here are the things that I don't understand:
- what does "running stan" mean?
- what's a "physical model"?
- how did you compile it into an executable file? 
- what's an "input file"? Is that data? Is that the Stan program?
...

There's a lot more that I'm not understanding.

It sounds like you want to use the Stan language to write a model that calls an external process. That isn't possible in the Stan language. It's possible to hack the generated C++ code to do whatever you want, but I wouldn't suggest it.

If you are looking for a different answer, could you ask the question with more detail / context?



Daniel
